device.note: The fused decoder stage, like the functional one, runs on a single Blackhole chip (1x1 mesh) as required by the skill.

implementation.dtype_layout_memory: BFLOAT16 weights/activations, TILE layout, DRAM interleaved (unchanged by the fusing stage); the decode residual stream is width-sharded in L1 across the layer so the hidden-size RMSNorms run multi-core, and the prefill dense projections use ttnn.experimental.minimal_matmul at or above 3072 rows (MINIMAL_MATMUL_MIN_ROWS) and ttnn.linear below, which is the measured crossover for the whole six-matmul chunk
implementation.kv_cache_sizing: full max_seq_len per user (no bounded sliding-window cache in this stage)

extra_persistent_buffers.formula: 2 (cos, sin) * 131072 positions * head_dim(128) * 2 bytes (BF16), TILE layout
extra_persistent_buffers.note: Added by the fusing stage so prefill hands rotary_embedding_hf a pre-tilized table. The ROW_MAJOR tables the functional stage already carried are still needed for the decode-time per-user ttnn.embedding gather, so a sliding layer now holds both layouts. full (NoPE) layers hold neither. This does not change any capacity limit: it is 67 MB against a 968 MB per-layer weight footprint on a 32 GB part.

prefill.reference_harness: reduced layer-level: the HF cache is filled with the K/V of every position before the compared block by the real MuseGlimmerTextAttention K/V path, then the real HF MuseGlimmerTextDecoderLayer runs that 32-query block against the full prefix. Two blocks are checked at 131072 - the last 32 rows and an interior block at row 65536 (first row of internal prefill chunk 9, entirely dependent on the 8th carried sliding window). A 131072-query HF forward is not tractable on CPU.

batch.note: Ragged per-user prompt lengths 2000..3147 (straddling the 2048 sliding window) and per-user decode positions in one batched call. batch=13 is prime and larger than the 11-wide device grid, so it has no batch-core rectangle and exercises the decode head-concat's shape-agnostic fallback.
batch.device_op_ceiling_source: ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/experimental/transformer/nlp_create_qkv_heads_decode/device/nlp_create_qkv_heads_decode_device_operation.cpp:45-51 hard-caps num_users at 32, so decode batch is capped at 32 by the op, not by this layer. The largest tested batch (32) is therefore also the largest supported one; prefill is per-user and has no such cap.

continuation_prefill.note: Two start_pos-separated prefill calls compared against a single-shot HF prefill, then a decode past the join. sliding layers require the caller to thread sliding_kv_tail; the 1024 and 64 splits give a tail shorter than the 2048 window.

sliding_window_control.note: Direct probe against an explicit torch kv_idx > cur_pos - W mask over a permuted paged cache; the prefill op's window is pinned separately by doc/functional_decoder/sdpa_sliding_window_chunk_repro.py. Owned by the functional stage; the fused decoder uses the same decode SDPA op and window.

nonzero_cache_slot.note: Multi-chunk prefill plus decode off cache slot 2, exercising page-table row slicing and the chunked paged read from a non-zero row.

notes: No capability reduction was taken by the fusing stage. The advertised 131072-token context is supported and tested end to end (paged prefill fill + paged decode read) for both decoder-layer kinds by the fused decoder, and the fused graph is measurably more accurate than the functional one it replaces at every tested length, kind, batch and context.

performance.note: Warmed, signposted Tracy windows; Device Time column from tt-perf-report --csv, microseconds. 8 trace replays per decode window; all ten committed captures (eight fused windows plus the two multi-chunk functional baselines) are free of dropped profiler markers. 'baseline' is the functional decoder measured the same way.
performance.context_scaling: sliding decode is context-independent (SDPA reads at most the 2048 window); full (NoPE) decode SDPA goes 36 us -> 529 us between 2048 and 131071.
performance.decode_roofline: One decode step streams 967,835,648 B of BF16 weights; at the 383 GB/s the six matmuls achieve that is 2.526 ms, i.e. 93 % of the 2.710 ms fused decode step. Further decode gains require moving fewer bytes (weight dtype) or a higher-efficiency matmul config.
performance.fidelity_policy: Unchanged from the functional stage: the prefill dense projections pin the same HiFi2 / fp32_dest_acc_en=False / packer_l1_acc=True compute-kernel config that ttnn.linear selects by default for BF16, so the before/after is a pure topology comparison. minimal_matmul's own default is more accurate (PCC 0.999994 vs 0.999947 vs FP32) and 2.3-2.5 ms slower per 8192-token prefill; that choice belongs to the optimized-decoder stage. ONE fidelity knob was turned: every RMSNorm runs HiFi4/math_approx_mode=False/fp32_dest_acc_en=True/packer_l1_acc=True instead of ttnn.rms_norm's own default (HiFi4/approx=True/fp32_acc=False/l1_acc=False, rmsnorm.cpp:16-20). Measured against float64: prefill norm 978.27 -> 991.78 us with max relative error 6.5e-2 -> 4.2e-3; sharded decode norm 15.53 -> 14.92 us (faster) and 1.0e-2 -> 4.8e-3. Cost ~54 us across the four hidden-size norms plus of order 25 us across the two per-head QK norms, i.e. 0.11-0.16 % of a 49,318 us prefill window, and nothing in decode; worth +3.3e-4 to +3.8e-4 of the accuracy gain where no matmul kernel changes (doc/fused_decoder/logs/norm_fidelity_control.log).

tests.accuracy_controls_note: All six prefill controls show the fused graph closer to the HF reference by +3.3e-4 to +1.2e-3 (the test allows no prefill regression at all). Five of six decode controls improve; one drifts by -4.6e-5, inside the 2e-4 BF16 re-association band the test allows for decode, which never changes matmul kernel. That band was 5e-4 until the prefill per-head QK norms took the same compute-kernel config as every other norm in the layer: those norms write the KV cache a decode step reads, and including them shrank the worst decode drift 10x.

capacity_probes_note: The listed probes were run by the functional stage against functional_decoder.py. The fusing stage does not re-run them: its own capacity evidence is stronger, because test_full_context_prefill_tail_pcc / test_full_context_decode_pcc run a real 131072-token paged prefill and a decode at position 131071 through the fused layer on device and compare against the HF reference, rather than only asserting the shapes fit.
